samples.summary: `mergeDropsHeadingMemory` added to the browser entry (`src/index.ts`) but not to the Node entry (`src/node.ts`), which `YorkieDocStore` resolves to under the Node integration lane
samples.evidence: packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts:38 imports `mergeDropsHeadingMemory` from '@wafflebase/docs'. packages/docs/package.json:14-26 gives that specifier a "node" condition resolving to ./dist/node.js, and packages/docs/src/node.ts:101-113 re-exports the block-helpers list WITHOUT `mergeDropsHeadingMemory` (only `applyMergeBlocks` at line 111). The comment at packages/docs/src/node.ts:95-100 states explicitly that `YorkieDocStore` imports these helpers from '@wafflebase/docs' and that the docs `.integration.ts` suite runs that store under Node, 'so the helpers must be re-exported here as well. Kept in sync with the browser entry (src/index.ts).' The store is loaded under Node by packages/frontend/tests/helpers/two-user-docs-yorkie.ts:2 (`import { YorkieDocStore } from '@/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts'`), used by packages/frontend/tests/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store-concurrent.integration.ts:13, run via `tsx --test "tests/**/*.integration.ts"` (packages/frontend/package.json:16). An ESM named import that the module does not export fails at load time, so every Yorkie docs integration test file would fail to load, not just the merge case. No tsconfig path alias in packages/frontend/tsconfig.json redirects '@wafflebase/docs' to source. Fix belongs in packages/docs/src/node.ts: add `mergeDropsHeadingMemory` to the re-export block.

samples.summary: Paste reaches the same 'heading memory travels onto text that was never a heading' defect the new merge guard closes, without passing through it
samples.evidence: The delta establishes the provenance rule that a `list-item`'s remembered `headingLevel` must not survive when foreign text is folded into the block (`mergeDropsHeadingMemory`, block-helpers.ts:279). The paste path bypasses it: packages/docs/src/view/text-editor.ts:3575-3580 appends the pasted inlines to the existing head block and then unconditionally sets `headBlock.type = firstPasted.type` and `headBlock.headingLevel = firstPasted.headingLevel`; the same happens for the tail block at lines 3604-3607. `copySelectedBlocks` copies the memory verbatim for a partial slice (text-editor.ts:3404: `if (block.headingLevel !== undefined) cloned.headingLevel = block.headingLevel;`), so pasting a bulleted heading into a paragraph makes the paragraph a `list-item` carrying a heading level, and the block's own pre-existing body text is then promoted to a Heading N on un-listing — exactly the #783 follow-up symptom. Confirming needs a paste round-trip test; the write path is unguarded either way. Fix could live either at these two assignments or by routing them through the same helper.

verdict.reason: The finding is real and reachable as described. The new provenance rule is `mergeDropsHeadingMemory` (block-helpers.ts:279-285, doc comment 268-278: a remembered heading level "must not travel onto the incoming body text — otherwise removing the list promotes text that was never a heading"), applied in `applyMergeBlocks` (block-helpers.ts:293) and mirrored in yorkie-doc-store.ts:2187. The multi-block paste path bypasses it verbatim as quoted: text-editor.ts:3575-3582 splices pasted inlines onto the existing head block (which retains its own caret-preceding text) and then unconditionally sets `headBlock.type = firstPasted.type` and `headBlock.headingLevel = firstPasted.headingLevel`; text-editor.ts:3604-3611 does the same for the tail block. A `list-item` carrying `headingLevel` is a real model state, deliberately created at memory.ts:257-262 when a heading is bulleted, and copied verbatim for partial slices at text-editor.ts:3404. `unlistedBlockType` (model/types.ts:337-344) then promotes any list-item with a `headingLevel` back to a heading, so the head block's pre-existing body text becomes a Heading N on un-listing — the exact symptom the merge guard was added to prevent. The path is reachable from three live paste handlers (text-editor.ts:1118, 1147, 1218), and no other normalization intervenes: the only `headingLevel` writes in text-editor.ts are lines 1032, 2310, 3404, 3578, 3607. This is in the blast-radius lane (a newly formalised invariant with another entry point reaching the same state outside the diff), and major is the right severity. Only inaccuracy is the method name — it is `getSelectedBlocks`, not `copySelectedBlocks` — but the cited line 3404 and its content are correct, which does not affect the substance.
